issues.title: Session without context manager usage
issues.description: The rule requires all database sessions to use 'with Session(db.engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:' pattern for proper resource management, but the code creates a session without a context manager and never closes it
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
session = Session(db.engine)
row = session.scalar(stmt)
if not row:
    raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
session.commit()
issues.rule_name: SQLAlchemy Sessions Must Use Context Managers

issues.title: Database transaction commits called on every variable update instead of batched
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer now calls flush() inside the loop for each updated conversation variable, rather than batching all updates and flushing once after the loop completes. This causes multiple unnecessary database commits when multiple conversation variables are updated in a single node execution, significantly degrading performance and creating database contention. The original implementation correctly tracked whether any updates occurred with the `updated_any` flag and only flushed once after all updates were queued.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence layer registered before persistence layer causing event ordering issue
issues.description: The conversation_variable_layer is now registered before the persistence_layer in the graph engine layer stack. In event-driven architectures with layered middleware, the order of layer registration determines the order in which layers receive and process events. By registering conversation_variable_layer first, it will receive and process NodeRunSucceededEvent events before the persistence_layer has a chance to persist the node execution state. This creates a race condition where conversation variables might be updated in the database before the corresponding node execution is persisted, leading to data inconsistency if failures occur between the two operations.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence failures are silently ignored
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer calls update() without catching exceptions, relying on the graph engine's blanket exception handler which logs but continues execution. When persistence fails (e.g., database errors, ConversationVariableNotFoundError), the exception is caught by the engine's try-except in event_manager.py, logged, and execution continues. This creates silent data loss where the in-memory variable pool contains updated values but the database doesn't, causing data inconsistency. In the original implementation, these errors would fail the node execution and stop the workflow, providing clear feedback to users.

issues.title: ConversationVariable query missing tenant_id filter
issues.description: The SELECT against the tenant-scoped ConversationVariable table is filtered by id and conversation_id only, with no tenant_id predicate. This violates the requirement that tenant-scoped queries must include tenant_id scoping to prevent cross-tenant data access.
issues.rule_name: Database Queries Must Include tenant_id Scoping

issues.title: Missing return type annotation on __init__
issues.description: The __init__ method is missing an explicit return type annotation (e.g., "-> None"), which violates the requirement that all Python function definitions include type annotations for parameters and return values.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: def __init__(self, variables: dict[tuple[str, str], object] | None = None):
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30531 - feat: Add conversation variable persistence layer

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves conversation-variable database writes out of the Variable Assigner v1/v2 nodes and into a new graph-engine layer, `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`. The layer listens for `NodeRunSucceededEvent`s from `VARIABLE_ASSIGNER` nodes, reads the updated variables from `process_data`, and calls `ConversationVariableUpdater.update()`. It is registered only in `AdvancedChatAppRunner`. The updater implementation is moved from `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, the `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` protocol becomes selector-based, and the node tests are rewritten to check `process_data` instead of mocked DB calls.

The separation of concerns is a good idea: nodes stop reaching into the database and the import-linter exemption goes away. However, the move changes failure semantics in a way that breaks the data-integrity guarantee the node used to provide. The engine's `_notify_layers` swallows layer exceptions, so a failed conversation-variable write now results in a SUCCEEDED node, an updated in-memory pool, and a silently stale database. The debugger's single-step path also no longer persists anything because no layer is attached there. I'd request changes on those two points, plus the unclosed session and the vacuous skip test.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two high-severity issues drive this. First, persistence errors in the layer are logged and dropped by the event manager, so a DB failure silently diverges the conversation variable from the in-memory pool; before this change the node failed the run. Second, single-step debugger runs bypass the graph engine and attach no layer, so assigner nodes stop persisting conversation variables in the debugger, which previously worked. The unclosed `Session` and the vacuous skip test are medium issues that should be fixed in the same pass.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `VariableAssignerNode` v1 and v2 each called `conversation_variable_updater_factory()` inside `_run()` and wrote updated conversation variables to the database before returning. The node therefore owned the DB write, and a failure failed the node. The graph engine dispatches events to registered `GraphEngineLayer`s (for example `PersistenceLayer` and `PausePersistenceLayer`) through `event_manager._notify_layers`, and that dispatch catches and logs layer exceptions.

This PR removes the write from both nodes and adds `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` in `core/app/layers/`. The advanced-chat runner registers it ahead of the persistence layer. The layer reads `process_data` from each successful assigner event, filters for the `conversation` selector prefix, and calls the updater. The updater moves to `services/`. The read-only variable pool protocol is changed to a selector-based `get`, so the layer can read the pool through the same wrapper the other layers use.
steps: Entry point: `AdvancedChatAppRunner` builds the `workflow_entry` graph engine and now registers `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` before `PersistenceLayer` (app_runner.py ~L204-208). No other runner registers it.
Nodes: `VariableAssignerNode` v1 and v2 now compute the updated variables and store them in `process_data` only. The DB writes and the conversation-id checks are removed from both nodes.
Event path: when a node finishes, the engine emits `NodeRunSucceededEvent`. `_notify_layers` calls each layer's `on_event`, and any exception raised there is caught and logged rather than propagated.

Layer: `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer.on_event` filters for assigner success events, skips when there is no conversation id, and for each `conversation.*` selector reads the pool and calls `update` then `flush`.

Storage: `services/conversation_variable_updater.py` provides `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl`, which upserts the `ConversationVariable.data` row. `services/conversation_service.py` reuses the same factory for API-driven updates.

Gap: single-step runs (`WorkflowEntry.single_step_run`, used by `services/workflow_service.py`) call `node.run()` directly with no graph engine or layers, so debugger assigner runs no longer persist conversation variables.

findings.title: Layer persistence failures are swallowed, leaving the DB out of sync with a SUCCEEDED node
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` (`on_event`, around lines 45-53), a failed conversation-variable DB write is swallowed by `event_manager._notify_layers` in `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/event_management/event_manager.py`, so the node still reports SUCCEEDED while the DB is stale. Restore fail-fast behavior for this write. Options: move the persistence back into the node result path, or have the layer record the exception and abort the run through `self.command_channel`. Keep the write atomic per event, so a failure on one selector does not silently skip the rest. Add a unit test asserting that an updater exception stops the run or is surfaced, not just logged.

findings.title: Debugger single-step runs no longer persist conversation variables
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py`, `single_step_run` (around lines 121-200) calls `node.run()` with no graph engine or layers, so `VariableAssignerNode` no longer persists conversation variables in debugger single-step runs (`services/workflow_service.py` ~L696). Restore that behavior: either have the single-step path call the updater directly for assigner results when `invoke_from` is DEBUGGER, or attach `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` to the single-step flow. Use `conversation_variable_updater_factory` from `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, as `services/conversation_service.py` does. Verify with a test that a single-step assigner run updates the `ConversationVariable` row.

findings.title: Missing conversation_id now silently skips persistence; ConversationIDNotFoundError is dead
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` `on_event` (around lines 34-36), a None `conversation_id` makes the layer return silently even when the assigner wrote a conversation variable. Before this PR, v1 raised `VariableOperatorNodeError` and v2 raised `ConversationIDNotFoundError` (except for DEBUGGER). Decide the behavior explicitly. Either fail the write as before, or log at warning when conversation variables are being assigned without a conversation id. If the error is kept, remove the now-unused `ConversationIDNotFoundError` in `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/exc.py`, or reuse it. Add a unit test for the None-conversation-id branch.

findings.title: Database session is never closed in ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` (lines 14-23) creates `Session(db.engine)` without closing it, which leaks a DB connection on every call, including the not-found error path. Restore the context-manager form that the original `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` used: `with Session(db.engine) as session:` wrapping the select, the not-found check, the assignment, and `commit()`. Keep the `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` raise inside the block. No change to the public signature is needed.

findings.title: Vacuous test: the non-conversation-variable skip test cannot fail for the branch it names
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, `test_skips_non_conversation_variables` (around lines 122-144) builds an empty `MockReadOnlyVariablePool`, so the layer never reaches the prefix guard. The test passes even if the `selector[0] != CONVERSATION_VARIABLE_NODE_ID` check is removed. Seed the pool with a real `StringVariable` under the `environment` selector, so that the only reason `update` is not called is the prefix guard. Also rename `test_skips_when_outputs_missing` to match its behavior (empty `process_data`).

findings.title: Coverage gaps for error, None-id, and invalid-selector branches
findings.body:
The new layer tests cover the happy path, a non-assigner node, empty `process_data`, and (vacuously, see above) non-conversation selectors. They do not cover the `conversation_id is None` return, the `len(selector) < 2` warning branch, the case where `updater.update` raises, or the wiring in `AdvancedChatAppRunner`. The v1 and v2 node tests also lost their DB-write assertions, so nothing checks the end-to-end persistence path any more. Each of the branches above changes behavior, and none is exercised.

::code{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="22-36"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add unit tests to `api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` for `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer.on_event` in `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`. Cover: (1) `conversation_id` None leaves the updater untouched, matching the decided behavior; (2) a selector shorter than two elements logs a warning and is skipped; (3) when `updater.update` raises, the error is surfaced as decided in the persistence-failure fix. Follow the existing `Mock`/`MockReadOnlyVariablePool` helpers already in the file.

findings.title: updater.flush() is called once per variable instead of once per batch
findings.body:
`on_event` calls `self._conversation_variable_updater.flush()` inside the `for item in updated_variables` loop, so each variable triggers a flush. The `ConversationVariableUpdater` protocol says `update` may buffer and `flush` persists the buffer, which means batching was the intent. Calling flush per item defeats batching, and if a future updater buffers, the first flush can persist a partial set. Move the flush after the loop, as the old node did.

::code{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="38-53"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` `on_event` (lines 38-53), `flush()` runs inside the per-variable loop. The `ConversationVariableUpdater` protocol in `api/core/workflow/conversation_variable_updater.py` describes `flush` as persisting buffered updates, so it belongs after all `update` calls for the event. Dedent the `flush()` call to run once after the loop, and make sure it still runs when the loop does nothing useful.

findings.title: Redundant VariableAssignerNode v2 __init__ wrapper
findings.body:
The v2 node adds an `__init__` whose only job is to call `super().__init__` with the same four arguments. The base `Node.__init__` already has this signature, so the override is dead code and makes the class look like it has custom construction. Remove it so the class inherits the base constructor, or add a comment if it is there to pin the signature for the node factory.

::code{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py" lines="56-68"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py`, the `VariableAssignerNode.__init__` override (lines 56-68) only forwards `id`, `config`, `graph_init_params`, and `graph_runtime_state` to `super().__init__`, which matches the base `Node.__init__` in `api/core/workflow/nodes/base/node.py`. Delete the override so the class inherits the base constructor. Confirm `DifyNodeFactory` still constructs the node, using the existing test `test_node_factory_creates_variable_assigner_node`.

findings.title: Persistence moved out of nodes, with the import-linter exemption removed
findings.body:
Taking the database write out of `VariableAssignerNode` means the node only computes results, and the `common.impl -> extensions.ext_database` exemption in `.importlinter` can be deleted. Nodes are also easier to unit-test without a DB stub. The `process_data` payload already carries the updated variables and the `common_helpers` helpers are reused, so the layer reads data the engine already records.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="88-101"}

findings.title: ReadOnlyVariablePool selector API change is applied consistently
findings.body:
The `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` protocol, the `ReadOnlyVariablePoolWrapper.get` implementation, and the test mock in `test_pause_state_persist_layer.py` all move to the same `get(selector, /)` shape, and the mock guards `len(selector) < 2`. I found no caller still using the old `(node_id, variable_key)` form. Making the selector positional-only also prevents keyword drift.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/runtime/read_only_wrappers.py" lines="18-22"}
